subject: Request: Procedural evidence for 'no-derivative-modeling' promise and retention/deletion nuances
messages:
From: Jake Morris <jake.morris@acmehealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request: no-derivative-modeling promise + deletion proof

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the earlier call. Our security team needs written procedural evidence that Redwood will not use Acme Health data to train or improve models (including any derivative-modeling or fine-tuning pipelines). They also want clarification on retention windows for logs, snapshots, and any transient caches (KV cache, prefix cache) and an example deletion audit showing an actual customer-delete flow.

Specifically we need:
- A short technical/process document that explains how you prevent customer data from entering training datasets (controls, automated filters, and access controls).
- The retention SLAs for different stores (inference telemetry, request/response logs, backups, model snapshots).
- One redacted deletion audit CSV or report that demonstrates timestamps and S3 lifecycle/object deletion verification (we can redact customer identifiers).

Can you provide those artifacts this week? We have a review on Friday.

Cheers,
Jake
Security Engineer, Acme Health

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: no-derivative-modeling promise + deletion proof

On Mon, 29 Jun 2026 at 14:03, Priyom Das wrote:
> Team — forwarding Acme's request.

Attached are the artifacts I drafted: a two-page process explainer (redwood-no-derivative-modeling-process-2026-06.pdf) and a retention matrix (redwood-data-retention-matrix-2026.md). Highlights:

- Non-training controls: all inbound inference requests are tagged at ingress with a tenant_id. Production training pipelines operate on model training buckets that are air-gapped from inference logs; there is an automated validation job that rejects any dataset that contains tenant_id tags. Access to training buckets is IAM-restricted to a named training-team role, and changes to that IAM policy require SRE+Security approval via PR in our internal repo.

- Transient caches: runtime KV caches are ephemeral per instance and encrypted in-memory; they are not persisted to S3. Prefix caching is materialized only for performance in a dedicated cache cluster with TTLs set to minutes; those clusters have scheduled rolling restarts which clear in-memory state.

- Retention: inference telemetry (request/response) retained 30 days in hot store, 180 days in warm indexed store for debugging, then archived for up to 2 years for enterprise customers only (with opt-in). Backups/snapshots of model artifacts are retained per release policy (default 90 days) and are segregated from customer telemetry.

- Deletion audit: I exported a redacted S3 object lifecycle audit for a customer delete run (s3-deletion-audit-2026-06-30.csv). It includes object keys, delete-marker timestamps, and confirmation events from our object-store job that verifies tombstone creation. We can redact anything Acme flags.

Next steps: Karthik, please confirm the events included in the CSV are enough for their review and whether we should include MD5 or ETag rows. Vanessa, once you have the cover note I will iterate on tone and consolidate.

Attachments (stubbed):
- redwood-no-derivative-modeling-process-2026-06.pdf (process + tech controls)
- redwood-data-retention-matrix-2026.md (table mapping store -> retention)
- s3-deletion-audit-2026-06-30.csv (redacted sample)

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Jake Morris <jake.morris@acmehealth.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: no-derivative-modeling promise + deletion proof

Jake — thanks for the patience. Please find the requested artifacts attached (see filenames below). To summarize in plain terms: Redwood does not use customer inference traffic to train or fine-tune models. Inference logs are tagged and isolated; training datasets are curated from approved sources and are air-gapped from inference telemetry. Short-lived runtime caches are in-memory only and not persisted to training stores; persistent snapshots and backups are retained per the retention matrix and are segregated from customer telemetry.

Attachments included (redacted where appropriate):
- redwood-no-derivative-modeling-process-2026-06.pdf (process flow, automated checks, IAM controls, PR approvals required to add any dataset to training pipelines)
- s3-deletion-audit-2026-06-30.csv (redacted sample showing object delete markers and verification events)
- redwood-data-retention-matrix-2026.md (store-by-store retention windows and enterprise opt-in rows)

If Acme needs a live walkthrough of the deletion job (we can scrub logs in real time) or a short architecture diagram for their security team, happy to schedule 30 mins. Also note we can map the artifacts to specific contract clauses if you point us at the relevant section.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
